column4: The Holy Spirit is not a new spirit but is of God and has been with God since the very beginning. In Genesis 1:2 the Spirit of God is hovering on the waters during creation. In Nehemiah 9:20, the scriptures say that it was the Spirit who instructed the people in the wilderness. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God anointed the kings, judges, and prophets in the Old Testament. In Joel 2:28-29 the Spirit is promised to be poured out on all mankind. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God raised Jesus from the dead, and now dwells in us (Romans 8:11). There is only one Holy Spirit, and He has always been the same. How He works with people has looked different at different times, but His heart has never changed.

column4: The Holy Spirit is first and foremost, from and of God. The scriptures refer to the Spirit as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ, while these highlight different aspects, they are all one in the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and is holy (blameless, innocent, pure, not profane). Some translations refer to the Holy Spirit as the Holy Ghost.
column5: The Holy Spirit is first and foremost from God and belongs to God. The Scriptures refer to the Spirit as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ; although these highlight different aspects, they are all the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and holy (blameless, spotless, pure, not impure). In some translations the Holy Spirit is also referred to as the Holy Ghost.

column4: The word spirit in Greek is **Pneuma** (**NYOO-mah** - **G4151**), it means breath, or wind. The Hebrew word for spirit means the same. Breath is significant as we need it in constant supply to live. It was God's breath that He blew into Adam to bring Him to life, likewise it was Jesus' breath that He breathed last before He died on the cross. Without breath there is no life. Breath like wind can be felt and experienced but are not as easily observed as other ‘elements’ water, fire, earth.
column5: In Greek the word for spirit is **Pneuma** (**NYOO-mah** - **G4151**), which means breath, or wind. The Hebrew word for spirit has the same meaning. Breath is important because we need its constant supply to live. It was the breath that God breathed into Adam to give him life, and likewise, before dying on the cross, what Jesus exhaled for the last time was also breath. Without breath there is no life. Like air, breath can be felt and experienced, but it is not as easily seen as the other “elements” water, fire, earth.

column5: > **<u>Matthew 16:18</u>** (NKJV)\\n>\\n> And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.\\n>

column4: This is an amazing and comforting promise. Gates are fixed defensive armaments. When Jesus says that the *gates of hell shall not prevail*, He is painting the picture of a conquering army that knocks down the gates and captures the city!
column5: This is a wonderful and comforting promise. Gates are stationary defensive structures. When Jesus says that *the gates of hell cannot prevail*, He presents the picture of a victorious army smashing the gates and seizing the city!

column4: The Holy Spirit brings supernatural boldness to proclaim the witness of the Gospel in the face of persecution. The outcome of this empowerment can be described, but it's best experienced. It’s a supernatural (greater than human) boldness that motivates believers to share. This boldness of preaching is often accompanied by supernatural acts of demonstration of the Spirit and of power (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead raised, those tormented by evil spirits are set free, people with hard hearts turn and repent.
column5: The Holy Spirit gives supernatural boldness to proclaim the witness of the gospel in the face of persecution. The results of this empowerment can be described, but it is best to experience it. It is a boldness greater than human (supernatural), which compels believers to share. This boldness in preaching is often accompanied by supernatural works that demonstrate the Spirit and power (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead are raised, those tormented by evil spirits are set free, and the hard-hearted turn and repent.

column4: Jesus said these works and greater would we do! (John 14:12). These collective works are supernatural, divine, and desperately needed in a world tearing itself apart, miserable, full of pain, waiting for the mature sons of God to be made clearly manifest! (Romans 8:22-23)
column5: Jesus said that we will do these works and even greater ones! (John 14:12). These collective works are supernatural, divine, and are desperately needed in a world that is tearing itself apart, sorrowful, and full of pain, which is eagerly waiting for the mature sons of God to be revealed! (Romans 8:22-23)

column4: Jesus' chosen instrument for change on the earth is His church, empowered, emboldened, and directed by the Holy Spirit.
column5: The instrument Jesus has chosen for transformation on the earth is His church, empowered, emboldened, and guided by the Holy Spirit.

column4: ## Building a Relationship with the Holy Spirit
column5: ## Building a Relationship with the Holy Spirit

column4: Every relationship takes time and experience to develop deeply. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, our comforter, our helper, and our guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.
column5: Every relationship takes time and experience to develop deeply. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, our comforter, our helper, and our guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.

column4: Start to think of the Holy Spirit as you would a person. In our relationship we can both work to build it or do things that weaken our relationship. He can be ignored, He can be quenched, He can be blasphemed, or He can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.
column5: Begin to think of the Holy Spirit as a person. In our relationship we both can build it together, or we can do things that weaken the relationship. He can be ignored, He can be quenched, He can be blasphemed, or He can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.

column4: Don’t ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He is always speaking to us and the church. If you don’t yet know how to distinguish the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (like all healthy and beneficial relationships). But don’t worry, you already have built into you all the necessary parts needed to start to develop a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit.
column5: Do not ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He is always speaking to us and to the Church. If you do not yet know how to discern the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (as with all healthy and beneficial relationships). But do not worry, all the components necessary to begin developing a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit are already embedded within you.

column4: The quickest and most reliable ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit is to
column5: The quickest and most reliable ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit are

column4: 1.  Call out to Him **individually** in prayer, pause and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 1.  Call on Him in prayer, **personally**, pause, and wait until He speaks.

column4: 2.  Call out to Him as part of a **group** of people who know Him (the church), pause, and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 2.  Call on Him, together with a **group** of people who know Him (the Church), pause, and wait until He speaks.

column4: I use the phrase ‘call out’ to mean literally, with your mouth, or however you speak (with your hands if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth). Why speak? A few reasons:
column5: I use the phrase ‘call on’ literally: with your mouth, or in whatever way you speak (with your hands, if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth). Why speak? A few reasons:

column4: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in God's image. God speaks, and so do we.
column5: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in the image of God. God speaks, and we speak as well.

column4: 2.  We use speaking as the primary way to communicate. You can also write down what you want to say (journaling) and speak it aloud.
column5: 2.  We use speech as the primary means of communication. You can also write what you want to say (journaling) and speak it out loud.

column4: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act, and indicates to the party you are talking to, that you’d like to engage them in a conversation.
column5: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act, and it signals to the one you are talking to that you want to include them in the conversation.

column4: #### What should you say?
column5: #### What should you say?

column4: If you’ve never talked to God, try introducing yourself. Sure, it will feel a bit weird, but that discomfort is okay and temporary. Along with introducing yourself, tell God that you want to talk to Him and that you want Him to talk back to you.
column5: If you have never talked with God, try introducing yourself. Sure, it feels a bit awkward, but that awkwardness is okay and temporary. Along with your introduction, tell God that you want to talk with Him and that you want Him to answer you.

column4: Consider asking Him a question. It doesn’t have to be a deep theological question; it can start simple. Can you show me Your love for me? Why do I have a certain feeling? What would You like to tell me?
column5: Consider asking Him a question. It doesn’t have to be a deep theological question; you can start simple. Could you show me your love for me? Why am I feeling a certain way? What do you want to tell me?

column4: #### Then what?
column5: #### Then what?

column4: Well in all effective relationships you speak for a bit, then you pause and listen. God will speak.
column5: As in all effective relationships, you speak for a while, then pause and listen. God will speak.

column4: God speaks in many ways, but He wants to do it personally, and internally. It will likely not be an audible voice (like if your best friend was to say your name aloud) but it will be an internal voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah refers to this as the ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).
column5: God speaks in many ways, but He desires to speak personally and internally. It likely will not be an audible voice (as if your best friend shouted your name), but an inner voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah refers to it as a ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).

column4: The most common ways that I've personally witnessed God talk to people, and I've been blessed to help dozens of people learn how to talk to God directly, is some combination of the following:
column5: The most common ways God speaks with people that I have personally seen—and I have had the blessing of helping dozens of people learn to speak with God directly—are some combination of the following:

column4: - A knowing - the person talking to God gets an immediate understanding that helps them.
column5: - An ‘understanding’ - the person talking with God immediately receives a kind of insight that helps them.

column4: - A picture - also known in the scriptures as a vision or a dream (a vision is when you are awake, a dream is when you are asleep), God will give you a picture in your mind. Perhaps it’s a memory, or place you’ve been or know? Explore the picture, what do you see? What do you feel as a result? What’s happening?
column5: - An ‘image’ - in Scripture also known as a vision or a dream (a vision is when you are awake, a dream is when you are asleep), God will give you an image in your mind. Perhaps it is a memory, or a place you have been or know? Explore the image; what do you see? As a result of it, what do you feel? What is happening?

column4: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you can hear, and spoken into your heart and mind.
column5: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you can hear, speaking to your heart and mind.

column4: #### What will God say?
column5: #### What does God say?

column4: Not sure! But that’s the fun in it. I can say that He is NOT the spirit of fear, but of perfect love and that it will never violate the teaching of the scriptures. E.g., God will never tell you to commit an extra-marital affair.
column5: Not sure! But that’s the fun of it. I can say this: He is not a spirit of fear, but of perfect love, and He will never violate the teachings of Scripture. For example, God will never tell you to have an extramarital relationship.

column4: Now what?
column5: What now?

column4: Keep the dialogue going! It’s really that simple.
column5: Keep the conversation going! It really is that simple.

column4: ### Why build a relationship?
column5: ### Why build a relationship?

column4: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! The work goes much more smoothly if we have a shared language, and relationship with Him. Can you imagine trying to work with someone in your job if you had no relationship, did not speak the same language, and couldn't communicate?!
column5: The Holy Spirit is a Helper. A Helper helps us! If we have a shared language and relationship with Him, things move forward much more easily. Imagine, at your work, if you had no relationship with someone, couldn’t speak the same language, and couldn’t communicate at all—how would you work together?!

column4: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), we have built into us all already the natural abilities we need, but we may lack experienced proficiency.
column5: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep recognize His voice (John 10:27), the natural abilities we need are already built into us, but we may lack experiential proficiency.

column4: Speaking from personal experience, a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence brings us peace, comfort, and direction, but only if you know how to seek, listen, and obey Him.
column5: Speaking from personal experience, a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the finest parts of being a Christian. His presence gives us peace, comfort, and direction, but only when you know how to seek Him, listen, and obey.

column4: Develop a sensitivity with the Holy Spirit. Like many married people over time, you can communicate with your spouse in a unique way and sometimes just through a look. The look alone tells you everything you need to know about what just happened and what's going to happen. Build that type of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Include Him in your whole life, this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will provide so much depth and richness to your walk of faith.
column5: Develop sensitivity to the Holy Spirit. Like many married people, over time you can communicate with your spouse in unique ways and sometimes even with just a glance. That glance alone tells you everything you need to know about what just happened and what is about to happen. Build that same kind of sensitivity and intimacy with the Holy Spirit. Involve Him in your whole life; this is a wonderful aspect of your relationship with Him that will provide great depth and richness to your journey of faith.

column4: The Holy Spirit has come to lead us and guide us, to empower us to be God’s people, and to see the people of the Earth radically transformed, delivered from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Getting to know him, building trust with Him is essential to everyday life and to accomplish the work that Jesus has for us to do.
column5: The Holy Spirit has come to lead and guide us, to empower us to become God’s people, and to see the people of the earth saved from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light, fundamentally transformed. Knowing Him and building trust with Him are essential for daily life and for accomplishing the work Jesus has given us to do.

column4: ## Personal Reflection Questions
column5: ## Personal Self-Reflection Questions

column4: 1.  How have you experienced the Holy Spirit as your Comforter, Guide, or source of power? Which role resonates most with your current season of life?
column5: 1.  How have you experienced the Holy Spirit as your Comforter, Guide, or source of power? Which of these roles best aligns with the current season of your life?

column4: 2.  Reflect on the difference between the Holy Spirit being “within” (inward work) and “upon” (outward work). How does this distinction impact your understanding of His work in your life?
column5: 2.  Reflect on the difference between the Holy Spirit being “within” (internal work) and “upon” (external work). How does this distinction affect your understanding of His work in your life?

column4: 3.  What steps can you take to cultivate a deeper relationship with the Holy Spirit and recognize His voice more clearly?
column5: 3.  What steps can you take to develop a deeper relationship with the Holy Spirit and recognize His voice more clearly?

column5: 4.  We must rely on the power of the Holy Spirit to move forward boldly and to fulfill the mission God has given us. What specific mission and focus has God given you?

column5: 1.  **Icebreaker question:** “When you think about the Holy Spirit, what is the first word or image that comes to your mind? Why?”

column5: 2. **Scripture Exploration:** John 14:26 Read. As Teacher and Helper, how does the role of the Holy Spirit encourage you in your journey of faith?

column5: 3.  **Holy Spirit within vs. upon:** Discuss the difference between the Holy Spirit being “within” for transformation and “upon” for empowerment. Why are both aspects essential for a believer?

column5: 4.  **Practical guidance:** How can we practically position ourselves to hear the voice of the Holy Spirit in daily decisions and follow His leading?

column5: 5.  **Reflection**: Think of a time when you felt empowered to act by the Holy Spirit. How did that experience affect your faith and the people around you?
